Run LPE-ANOVA

Source: R/LPE_ANOVA.R
LPE_ANOVA.Rd

Performs multi-group (and multi-way, interaction-free) differential expression analysis using an intensity-dependent local pooled error variance trend.

Usage

LPE_ANOVA(
  object,
  n.bin = 100,
  df = 10,
  trim.method = c("auto", "dvalue", "iqr", "none"),
  use_weighted_between = "auto",
  d.threshold = 1.2,
  analysis.method = c("LPE", "standard_anova", "auto"),
  standard.min.group.n = 5,
  verbose = TRUE,
  p.method = c("chisq", "F_inf"),
  variance.eval = c("grand_mean", "per_group"),
  variance.trend = c("pooled", "per_group")
)

Arguments

object

A list returned by LPE_preprocess().

n.bin

Number of quantile bins used for variance trend estimation.

df

Degrees of freedom for smoothing spline.

trim.method

Outlier trimming method applied to pairwise values used for variance trend estimation. One of "auto" (default), "dvalue", "iqr", or "none". "auto" chooses by replication (see Automatic variance-training settings in Details): "none" when every design cell has at least two samples, otherwise "dvalue". See LPE_ANOVA_var for the trimming rules.

use_weighted_between

"auto" (default), TRUE or FALSE. Whether to include weighted between-group differences in variance trend estimation. "auto" uses FALSE when every design cell has at least two samples (replicate pairs only), otherwise TRUE.

d.threshold

Numeric. Threshold on the LPEseq1 raw-D scale, used to derive the fixed M-scale cutoff (d.threshold/sqrt(2)) applied when trim.method = "dvalue". Default 1.2, matching the default reported in LPEseq1 (Gim et al. 2016). Ignored for other trim.method values. See LPE_ANOVA_var for details.

analysis.method

Analysis method. One of "LPE", "standard_anova", or "auto". "LPE" uses the local pooled error-based ANOVA. "standard_anova" uses conventional gene-wise ANOVA (Type II sums of squares for multi-way designs). "auto" selects standard ANOVA when every factor-level combination (design "cell") has at least standard.min.group.n samples; otherwise, LPE-ANOVA is used.

standard.min.group.n

Minimum per-cell sample size required to use standard ANOVA when analysis.method = "auto". A "cell" is a unique combination of the design factor levels (for a one-way design, this is simply a group).

verbose

Logical. Whether to print progress messages.

p.method

P-value calculation method. One of "chisq" or "F_inf".

variance.eval

Character string specifying how the fitted variance trend is evaluated for the test statistic. One of "grand_mean" or "per_group". "grand_mean" (default) evaluates the variance trend once at each gene's overall (grand) mean expression and uses it as a single pooled variance for the test statistic; this mode supports both one-way and multi-way (main-effects-only) designs. "per_group" evaluates the variance trend separately at each group's mean expression and combines the group-specific variances via inverse-variance weighting into a Welch-type unequal-variance test statistic (returned with method = "LPE_Welch" and a different var/MS_between definition; see Details). "per_group" is only supported for one-way designs (a single design term); it raises an error for multi-way designs.

variance.trend

Character string specifying which variance trend is read for each group when variance.eval = "per_group". One of "pooled" (default) or "per_group". "pooled" reads every group's variance from the single trend estimated from all design cells (behaviour of previous versions). "per_group" fits a separate variance trend for every group with at least two samples, using only that group's replicate pairs, as in LPEseq1 and the original LPE method; groups with a single sample read their variance from the pooled trend. Only used with variance.eval = "per_group"; requesting "per_group" together with variance.eval = "grand_mean" raises an error. See Details.

Value

A data.frame containing gene-level test statistics. For a one-way design, columns are unsuffixed (MS_between, F, p.value, q.value, ...), matching previous versions. For a multi-way design (e.g. design = ~ A + B), one main-effect test is reported per design term, with columns suffixed by the term name (e.g. F_A, p.value_A, q.value_A, F_B, p.value_B, q.value_B, ...); gene, mean, var, and method are shared across terms. The selected analysis method is stored in attr(result, "analysis.method"), and the design term names are stored in attr(result, "design.terms"). For LPE-ANOVA, trimming information, variance trend information, bin-level variance points, and the fitted variance trend object are stored in attr(result, "trim.info"), attr(result, "trend.info"), attr(result, "base.var"), and attr(result, "var.spline"). The variance-training settings actually used (after resolving "auto") are stored in attr(result, "variance.settings"). With variance.trend = "per_group", the group-specific trends and their bin-level variance points are stored in attr(result, "var.spline.group") and attr(result, "base.var.group") (named by group; NULL for groups that used the pooled trend), and the trend used by each group is recorded in attr(result, "variance.settings")$trend.source.

Details

Automatic variance-training settings. With the defaults trim.method = "auto" and use_weighted_between = "auto", the pairwise values used to estimate the variance trend are chosen from the replication of the design cells (unique combinations of the design factor levels):

  • every cell has at least two samples: within-cell replicate pairs only, without trimming (use_weighted_between = FALSE, trim.method = "none"). Replicate pairs contain no treatment effect, so trimming them would only remove genuine noise and under-estimate the variance.

  • at least one cell has a single sample: within-cell pairs (if any) plus weighted between-group pairs with fixed-threshold trimming (use_weighted_between = TRUE, trim.method = "dvalue"), the non-replicate procedure of LPEseq1 (Gim et al. 2016).

This mirrors LPEseq1, which uses within-group replicate pairs without outlier removal whenever a group is replicated and the outlier-trimmed between-condition pairs only for non-replicated groups. A value given explicitly for either argument is always used as given.

Group-specific variance trends. With variance.eval = "per_group" and variance.trend = "per_group" (one-way designs only), the variance of group \(i\) is read from a trend \(\sigma^2_i(A)\) fitted to the replicate pairs of that group alone, evaluated at the group mean: $$w_{gi} = n_i / \hat\sigma^2_i(\bar y_{gi}), \qquad T_g = \sum_i w_{gi} (\bar y_{gi} - \bar y^w_g)^2 \sim \chi^2_{k-1}.$$ This follows LPEseq1 (Gim et al. 2016) and the original LPE method (Jain et al. 2003), which estimate a baseline error curve for each replicated condition, and allows the noise level to differ between conditions at the same expression intensity. The rules are:

  • a group with at least two samples uses its own trend, fitted with within-group pairs only. Trimming follows trim.method when it is given explicitly; with trim.method = "auto" no trimming is applied, because replicate pairs contain no treatment effect;

  • a group with a single sample uses the pooled trend (estimated as for variance.trend = "pooled", i.e. with weighted between-group pairs and D-value trimming under the automatic settings), as LPEseq1 does for non-replicated conditions;

  • if a group-specific trend cannot be fitted (too few valid pairwise values), that group falls back to the pooled trend with a warning.

When every group has a single sample, all groups use the pooled trend and the result equals variance.trend = "pooled". The test statistic itself is unchanged; only the trend each group's variance is read from differs.

Multi-way designs. For a multi-way design ~ A + B + ... (no interaction terms allowed), each design term's main effect is tested by comparing, per gene, the full additive model against the model with that term dropped: SS_term = RSS(reduced) - RSS(full), with df_term = rank(X_full) - rank(X_reduced). This is the standard Type II sum-of-squares decomposition, which for a main-effects-only model does not depend on term order. The intensity-dependent pooled variance (from the same LPE variance-trend spline used for one-way designs) is used as the common denominator for every term's test statistic. This reduces exactly to the original one-way LPE-ANOVA when the design has a single term.

Examples

testdat <- system.file("testdat", package = "LPEseq2")
read_counts <- function(f) as.matrix(read.csv(file.path(testdat, f),
                                              row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE))
read_meta <- function(f) read.csv(file.path(testdat, f), row.names = 1)

## Two groups (6 vs 6), one-way design
prep2 <- LPE_preprocess(read_counts("LPEseq2_2group_test_counts.csv"),
                        read_meta("LPEseq2_2group_test_metadata.csv"),
                        design = ~ group, verbose = FALSE)
res2 <- LPE_ANOVA(prep2, verbose = FALSE)
head(res2[order(res2$p.value), ])
#>         gene     mean       var MS_between        F      p.value      q.value
#> 12 gene_0012 7.073082 0.2899427   18.05682 62.27719 2.983604e-15 2.983604e-12
#> 19 gene_0019 7.802183 0.2598390   13.35244 51.38738 7.582448e-13 3.791224e-10
#> 38 gene_0038 7.117452 0.2878370   14.11076 49.02344 2.529213e-12 8.430709e-10
#> 22 gene_0022 7.010981 0.2934340   13.66770 46.57846 8.802260e-12 2.200565e-09
#> 11 gene_0011 7.820358 0.2589403   11.78999 45.53169 1.501890e-11 3.003780e-09
#> 24 gene_0024 7.448984 0.2759103   10.95124 39.69129 2.974497e-10 4.957495e-08
#>    method
#> 12    LPE
#> 19    LPE
#> 38    LPE
#> 22    LPE
#> 11    LPE
#> 24    LPE
sum(res2$q.value < 0.05)
#> [1] 82
attr(res2, "variance.settings")$rule
#> [1] "within-group (replicate) pairs only, no trimming (smallest cell n = 6)"

## Welch-type statistic with group-specific variance trends
res2_pg <- LPE_ANOVA(prep2, variance.eval = "per_group",
                     variance.trend = "per_group", verbose = FALSE)
attr(res2_pg, "variance.settings")$trend.source
#>     Control Treatment_A 
#>       "own"       "own" 

## Three groups with a batch factor, additive design ~ group + batch
prep3 <- LPE_preprocess(read_counts("LPEseq2_test_counts.csv"),
                        read_meta("LPEseq2_test_metadata.csv"),
                        design = ~ group + batch, verbose = FALSE)
res3 <- LPE_ANOVA(prep3, verbose = FALSE)
head(res3[order(res3$p.value_group), ])
#>         gene     mean       var MS_between_group  F_group p.value_group
#> 11 gene_0011 7.383532 0.2868123         9.580432 33.40314  3.113159e-15
#> 12 gene_0012 6.888715 0.3068180         9.391096 30.60804  5.094461e-14
#> 38 gene_0038 6.802491 0.3119396         8.997715 28.84442  2.971858e-13
#> 19 gene_0019 7.543674 0.2804833         7.886401 28.11719  6.149783e-13
#> 22 gene_0022 6.711890 0.3181820         8.593651 27.00860  1.863438e-12
#> 25 gene_0025 8.482922 0.2395040         6.363551 26.56971  2.890156e-12
#>    q.value_group MS_between_batch    F_batch p.value_batch q.value_batch method
#> 11  3.113159e-12       0.21966581 0.76588690    0.38149249     0.9983678    LPE
#> 12  2.547231e-11       0.02524831 0.08229086    0.77421659     0.9983678    LPE
#> 38  9.906192e-11       0.07251272 0.23245758    0.62970753     0.9983678    LPE
#> 19  1.537446e-10       0.10840430 0.38649114    0.53414960     0.9983678    LPE
#> 22  3.726877e-10       0.07196450 0.22617398    0.63437539     0.9983678    LPE
#> 25  4.816926e-10       0.75357457 3.14639711    0.07609481     0.7939179    LPE

## Expected results shipped with the package
expected <- read.csv(file.path(testdat, "LPEseq2_2group_expected_results.csv"))
all.equal(res2$p.value, expected$p.value)
#> [1] TRUE
